subject: Urgent: Hosted API p95/p99 spike — production impact for Hedgerow
messages:
From: Daniel Brooks <daniel@hedgerow.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike — p99 regressions since 6/18 (production)

Hi Marissa,

We've had a production incident starting Saturday evening where p95 and p99 latencies for calls to the Redwood hosted text-generation endpoint jumped ~4-6x. This has affected our checkout flow (user-visible slowdowns) and we've seen a short burst of 503s. I've attached a short CSV with percentile timelines and a PNG of the metric chart.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2 (we're calling the hosted API there)
- SDK: hedgerow-node v2.1.0 (default timeout)
- Spike first observed: 2027-06-18 20:02 UTC
- Current: intermittent but recurring p99 ~1.8s (was ~350ms)

Can your team confirm whether this is a Redwood server-side regression or something on our side? We need an executive summary for our COO ASAP.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Brooks
Director of Engineering, Hedgerow

Attachments: hedgerow-p99-timeline.csv (text/csv), hedgerow-p99-graph.png (image/png)

Hi Marissa / Daniel — quick update from my side while Neha pulls deeper traces.

What we see from the control plane metrics: overall host-side token generation latency is not showing a cluster-wide regression for the model variant you're hitting. There is a correlated increase in 5xxs during the same windows Daniel called out, but digging into request logs we observe an unusual number of duplicate requests coming from the same Hedgerow API keys in short succession.

Hypothesis (working): client-side timeouts + SDK retry semantics are amplifying a small number of slow responses into many back-to-back retries, which then shows up as elevated p95/p99 and apparent rate pressure that can lead to transient 503s.

Action items:
- I'm attaching a quick extract of request IDs and timestamps (hedgerow-traces.txt) showing repeated requests with the same idempotency token within ~2s windows.
- Neha is going to analyze server-side timing and the exact timeout values returned by our frontdoor.
- Marissa — can you ask Hedgerow for the SDK version and local timeout config (they mentioned default, but we need exact values)?

I'll prepare a short note for the execs once we confirm root cause.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spike — root cause analysis (client timeouts + retry amplification)

Hi all — I pulled the traces and did a correlation between frontdoor logs and the Hedgerow request patterns. TL;DR: this is primarily client-side behavior, not a model runtime regression.

Findings:
- Frontdoor observed ~0.4% of requests for Hedgerow with server processing time > 800ms in the window. These slow responses alone would not explain a sustained p99 jump.
- In ~78% of the observed slow-response windows, Hedgerow's API key generated 2-5 near-duplicate requests within 1–3 seconds (same payload and idempotency token).
- Hedgerow uses hedgerow-node v2.1.0 which has a default request timeout of 1000ms and a retry backoff that immediately retries up to 3 times on timeout. That combination can convert a few 1s responses into many requests peaking together.
- Server-side traces show the frontdoor returned 504/timeout to the client at ~1.0s in several cases; the client retried immediately and so on. We also saw occasional queueing spikes at the load balancer during the amplified bursts which produced brief 503s.

Attached: hedgerow-traces.txt (request id timeline), hedgerow-p99-timeline.csv (percentile timeline).

Recommended next steps (customer-facing):
1) Ask Hedgerow to patch their SDK to v2.1.3 (we have a client-side fix that increases default timeout to 3000ms and adds jittered exponential backoff).
2) Add client-side idempotency enforcement or broaden idempotency token uniqueness if retries are expected.
3) Short-term mitigation: rate-limit rapid retries at the edge for the Hedgerow API key (we can apply a conservative token-based debounce rule) — ops can apply this within 30m.
4) Post-mortem & outbound executive summary for Hedgerow COO + offer of a one-time credit for the incident window.

I'll prepare a short exec summary once we decide on credits. If Hedgerow prefers, we can patch their SDK under an assisted-maintenance agreement.

Neha Kapoor
Engineering Manager, Infra Reliability
Redwood Inference

We've started the SDK patch (moving to v2.1.3 and turning on jittered backoff) and will roll it to production tonight.

A few asks from our side:

- Confirmation on the proposed short-term edge rate-limit (we expect minimal user impact if you debounce the retry bursts).
- Proposal for a one-time goodwill credit for the incident window.

Appreciate the help — this was fast.

Claire Ng
